title: Be Decisive: Noise-Induced Layouts for Multi-Subject Generation
role: Bounded Attention on SDXL with the boxes replaced by a layout read from the initial noise by a trained readout network; the box-free version of this loop's default fix
enters: a combination: cross-attention and self-attention, gated by a layout that must stay stable across early steps
enters_evidence: argument carried from Bounded Attention that attention layers blend similar subjects (p3), plus one qualitative example where a dove on an oscillating cluster boundary inherits a parrot's tail (Fig 5b); no measurement
changes: Bounded Attention masks in cross- and self-attention built from a predicted noise-induced layout, plus 5 gradient steps on the latent per step in the first 15 of 50 steps to keep each subject's region stable (loss = 0.3 L_cross + 0.21 L_var + 0.49 L_dice)
training: a readout network on SDXL decoder attention features is trained with a triplet loss on about 1,500 SDXL images segmented by GroundedSAM, 5,000 steps; no boxes, masks, LLM or reference image at sampling, but the subject nouns and count k must be known
model: SDXL (50 steps, DDPM, CFG 7.5; resolution not printed)
similar_subjects: user study, 25 prompts of 3 to 4 visually similar animals, 192 responses from 32 participants: probability a chosen image is this method's (0 to 1, 0.5 parity) 0.74 vs SDXL, 0.87 vs LLM+BA, 0.96 vs RPG, 0.89 vs Ranni, 0.9 vs LMD+; no two-animal split
which_pairs: not measured; only the argument from Bounded Attention that features of semantically similar subjects are blended in attention
when: not measured with numbers; argued that the initial noise fixes the layout (p1), shown qualitatively (Fig 2), subjects named after the first step and guidance confined to the first 15 of 50 steps
cost: about 77 s and 36 GB VRAM per image on an A100 against 7 s and 8 GB for plain SDXL; 5 gradient iterations per step for 15 steps (about 75 extra forward and backward passes, inferred)
headline: user preference on 3 to 4 similar animals: chosen image is this method's with probability 0.87 against LLM+BA and 0.74 against plain SDXL (0 to 1, 0.5 parity), SDXL
suggests: (inferred) box-free Bounded Attention on the same SDXL 50-step setting as CO3, at about 11 times the runtime and a trained readout network; also log how much the boundary between the two subjects' attention regions moves across the early steps as a fourth predictor
